specName: Shell-recorded manifests, so a full knowledge sync fits in one turn
last_action: 20/22 tasks done; 303/303 sync checks and 18/18 gates pass; T021 and T022 await the maintainer

FR-001.title: Sync MUST record each source through one procedure run that collects, measures and hashes its items and writes its manifest, so the agent types nothing into the manifest.

FR-002.title: The run that records a source MUST report each item's path and size to the agent, so budgeting and the index need no second measurement.

FR-003.title: The manifest MUST list every indexable item of the source, whatever the context budget, as today.

FR-004.title: Every file name and source value in the manifest MUST be escaped as JSON requires and MUST read back exactly as it is on disk or in the configuration.

FR-005.title: A file name MUST NOT run as a command, act as an option or create a file, as spec 007 requires.

FR-006.title: An item whose name is not valid UTF-8 MUST be left out of the manifest and the index, and the sync report MUST name every such item on one line under its source, as it names skipped symbolic links, with each byte that is not valid UTF-8 shown as \xHH.

FR-007.title: Recording and checking MUST apply the same item rules, every skip rule included, so a manifest the procedure has just written always passes the check.
tests: test-sync-git.sh --records::fresh manifest passes the check in every shell

FR-008.title: A manifest MUST appear whole or not at all: an interrupted sync MUST NOT leave a manifest that passes the check.

FR-009.title: The manifest MUST still be written last, after every item of the source is in place, so its write time keeps marking when the cache became valid.

FR-010.title: The manifest format MUST stay unchanged, its schema version included (see Verbatim Constraints), so search, status and every other reader keep reading it as today.

FR-011.title: The shared Cache Integrity Check MUST re-derive a source's records in one procedure run and report pass or fail, with no hash compared by the agent.

FR-012.title: Status, search, and sync's fallback and policy-fresh paths MUST use the one shared check by reference, and a source that fails it MUST be handled as corrupted, as today.

FR-013.title: A manifest written by an earlier version MUST either pass because its records match its files, or fail once and be rebuilt; it MUST NOT pass with records that do not match.

FR-014.title: The agent MUST still write the knowledge index, with budget allocation, conflict handling and messages unchanged.

FR-015.title: Recording and checking MUST need no tool beyond what the extension already declares and a standard macOS or Linux install provides.

FR-016.title: Recording and checking MUST behave the same under sh, bash and zsh, on macOS and on Linux back to Ubuntu 20.04 with git 2.25.

FR-017.title: The automated sync checks MUST cover recording with a hostile-name set that holds today's hostile names, every character JSON must escape (double quote, backslash, and every control character except line feed) and a name that is not valid UTF-8. Each check MUST confirm valid JSON, names that read back unchanged and no marker file, and that the name that is not valid UTF-8 is left out and shown with \xHH escapes.

FR-018.title: The README's troubleshooting section and the sync command MUST state that the first sync after an extension upgrade rebuilds every source, and that running sync again completes a sync that stopped part-way.

FR-019.title: The revision of spec 007's rule that the agent's file tool writes the manifest MUST be recorded with that decision, limited to the manifest; the index stays agent-written.

FR-020.title: Sync MUST treat a cache directory without a manifest or without its own git repository as an interrupted sync: remove it and clone again, so no git command ever acts on the project's own repository.

FR-021.title: With a freshness policy configured, a source whose manifest is missing MUST be refreshed, not skipped as fresh.
tests: test-sync-git.sh --recovery::freshness gate missing manifest is stale

decisions.decision: Compose three blocks per run: Indexable Items, new Item Records, and a record or check tail, run as one shell command per source
decisions.why: one definition of item rules and encoder, so record and check cannot drift; one agent step per source
decisions.rejected: a self-contained block per caller, or a script file (constitution I and III)

decisions.decision: Prefix sed, grep, sort, awk, od and tr with LC_ALL=C, never export it
decisions.why: macOS sed drops items after an invalid byte and GNU grep 3.4 prints Binary file matches in a UTF-8 locale; one byte order everywhere
decisions.rejected: keeping the user locale, or exporting LC_ALL into the agent's shell

decisions.decision: Leave out paths containing a line feed at find time with ! -path
decisions.why: a newline list cannot carry them; fragments created phantom and duplicate items
decisions.rejected: a -f guard plus de-duplication, which still lets a fragment shadow a real item

decisions.decision: Read links from git ls-files -s -z through tr
decisions.why: ls-files C-quotes names with quote, backslash or control bytes even with quotePath=false, so such links were indexed
decisions.rejected: decoding C-quoting in awk, or one ls-files call per item

decisions.decision: Encode names from od hex in one POSIX awk program: strict UTF-8 validation, JSON escapes, raw UTF-8 out via printf %c
decisions.why: awk only sees hex digits, so no awk variant can misread a hostile byte; BSD awk verified, spike checks mawk and gawk
decisions.rejected: ASCII-only \u escapes (kept as fallback), Python, jq or Perl (undeclared)

decisions.decision: Fix the manifest layout exactly and write it to .manifest.json.tmp then mv -f
decisions.why: whole-or-absent manifest with an mtime that marks validity; a canonical text the check can compare

decisions.decision: The check renders the manifest the record run would write, using the stored synced_at, and compares bytes; callers act on the verdict
decisions.why: byte equality proves valid JSON without a parser and cannot loop; status stays read-only
decisions.rejected: JSON parsing in awk, or header pattern matching

decisions.decision: Run the check in status step 2, search, both sync fallbacks and the policy-fresh path
decisions.why: status never ran the full check; the policy-fresh path trusted the manifest unchecked and had no sizes for step 7a

decisions.decision: Missing manifest is stale; warm path only with .git and .manifest.json, else remove the slug directory and clone
decisions.why: a failed clone left an empty directory from which git reached the user's project and ran checkout --force there; a missing manifest skipped every source under a policy
decisions.rejected: GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES alone, which stops the damage but never recovers the source

decisions.why: new behavior, same manifest format; old manifests fail once and are recorded again

decisions.decision: Item Records exports helpers (pick, render_manifest, print_report) that both tails reuse
decisions.why: one encoder and one renderer, so a manifest the record run writes always passes the check
decisions.rejected: duplicating the encoder in the check block

decisions.decision: Emit raw UTF-8 bytes from awk with printf %c under LC_ALL=C
decisions.why: verified on BSD awk 20200816 and mawk (byte-identical output); keeps names readable in the manifest and report
decisions.rejected: ASCII-only \u escapes, kept as the fallback if gawk ever differs

decisions.decision: Links filter strips the first tab-separated field with sub() instead of -F tab $2
decisions.why: a link name containing a tab was truncated at the tab

decisions.decision: Verify the Linux encoder row with a git-free cross-check against macOS output
decisions.why: images with git timed out and the internal apt mirror returned 520; mawk, dash, GNU grep and ext4 were the riskiest cells
decisions.rejected: public ports.ubuntu.com apt or recreating the user's podman machine

plan.summary: Plan: record and check runs composed from command blocks, hex-fed awk encoder, canonical atomic manifest, check by render-and-compare, two recovery fixes, spike first
plan.key_finding: 1.9.1 can run git checkout --force on the user's own project after a failed clone, and a freshness policy skips every source after an upgrade

implement.summary: Shell-recorded manifests shipped in the commands: record run, check block, recovery fixes; harness 229 -> 303 green; 2 maintainer tasks open

approach: One shell run per source composes Indexable Items, a new Item Records block and a tail. The record tail writes a canonical manifest atomically; the check tail renders the same text with the stored timestamp and compares bytes. Names reach a single POSIX awk encoder as od hex under LC_ALL=C, and two recovery bugs (failed-clone directory, missing-manifest freshness) are fixed alongside.
